# Third-party reference notes

- Creators' App iOS BLE architecture — `docs/creators-app-ios-ble-research.md` (creators-app-ios-ble-research.md lines 40-104): records readable CoreBluetooth wrapper, advertisement, and app-side pairing-state symbols from `data/Payload/Creators App.app/Frameworks/IEMBLEModule_ios.framework/IEMBLEModule_ios`; implementation bodies are encrypted.
- Creators' App pairing constant — `docs/creators-app-ios-ble-research.md` (creators-app-ios-ble-research.md lines 106-129): identifies `06 08 01 00 00 00 00` in the BLE framework executable's unencrypted initializer storage at file offsets `0x2c240..<0x2c247`; the destination EE01 mapping remains existing project evidence, not recovered IPA control flow.
- Creators' App connection and background limits — `docs/creators-app-ios-ble-research.md` (creators-app-ios-ble-research.md lines 131-159): indexes `data/Payload/Creators App.app/en.lproj/Localizable.strings` pairing/recovery instructions and `Info.plist` background declarations without treating them as proof of runtime ordering, timeout values, or reconnect policy.

- Modern Sony BLE location UUID map — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/vendors/sony/SonyGattSpec.kt` (SonyGattSpec.kt lines 18-68): defines DD01/DD11/DD21/DD30-DD33 and EE01 with access roles matching the A7C II GATT map.
- Modern Sony DD11 encoder — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/vendors/sony/SonyProtocol.kt` (SonyProtocol.kt lines 181-250): implements the matching 91/95-byte big-endian packet, UTC timestamp, timezone/DST fields, and DD21 bit check.
- Modern Sony location lifecycle — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/vendors/sony/SonyConnectionDelegate.kt` (SonyConnectionDelegate.kt lines 156-341): subscribes DD01, writes DD30 then DD31, reads DD32/DD33/DD21, and cleans up DD31 then DD30.
- Sony DD11 write policy — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/vendors/sony/SonyConnectionDelegate.kt` (SonyConnectionDelegate.kt lines 76-151): writes DD11 with response and up to three retries after encoding according to DD21.
- Sony advertisement parser — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/vendors/sony/SonyCameraVendor.kt` (SonyCameraVendor.kt lines 25-29 and 80-104): parses company `0x012D`, little-endian camera type `0x0003`, protocol-version byte 2, and unlock threshold 65.
- Sony pairing implementation — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/vendors/sony/SonyProtocol.kt` (SonyProtocol.kt lines 174 and 259) and `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/data/repository/KableCameraRepository.kt` (KableCameraRepository.kt lines 363-396): produces and writes the seven-byte EE01 payload with response.
- Sony pairing lifecycle — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/pairing/PairingViewModel.kt` (PairingViewModel.kt lines 296-349): performs EE01 on a transient vendor-pairing connection and disconnects after success, so later location sync does not require EE01 in the same BLE connection.
- CameraSync provenance — `third_party/CameraSync/docs/sony/README.md` (README.md lines 1-13): attributes its Sony BLE material to decompiled Creators' App code and named public reverse-engineering projects.
- CameraSync model-scope caveat — `third_party/CameraSync/docs/sony/FIRMWARE_UPDATES.md` (FIRMWARE_UPDATES.md lines 307-322): lists A7C II only for general app connectivity/firmware coverage and does not prove a physical A7C II DD11 test.
- CameraSync packet tests — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/test/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/vendors/sony/SonyProtocolTest.kt` (SonyProtocolTest.kt lines 156-379): tests packet size, header, byte order, coordinates, UTC conversion, and timezone fields but is not independent camera evidence.
- CameraSync flow tests — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/test/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/vendors/sony/SonyConnectionDelegateTest.kt` (SonyConnectionDelegateTest.kt lines 63-234): tests mocked DD30/DD31/DD11 order, DD01 subscription, retries, and DD21-selected packet size.
- CameraSync documentation error — `third_party/CameraSync/docs/sony/BLE_STATE_MONITORING.md` (BLE_STATE_MONITORING.md lines 317-321): the untested pairing table omits one trailing zero and conflicts with its own seven-byte production payload and the A7C II-accepted EE01 value.
- CameraSync documentation error — `third_party/CameraSync/docs/sony/BLE_STATE_MONITORING.md` (BLE_STATE_MONITORING.md lines 342-365): the text states `<tag> <00> <data>`, but its examples and bit table use `<tag> <data> <reserved-zero>`.
- CameraSync documentation error — `third_party/CameraSync/docs/sony/DATETIME_GPS_SYNC.md` (DATETIME_GPS_SYNC.md lines 12-15): labels both bytes after device type as reserved even though production uses the first as protocol version and only the second is reserved.
- CameraSync documentation error — `third_party/CameraSync/docs/sony/DATETIME_GPS_SYNC.md` (DATETIME_GPS_SYNC.md lines 109-142): labels DD11 values `0x005D` and `0x0059` as total lengths even though they are payload lengths 93/89 for total packets of 95/91 bytes.
- CameraSync lifecycle caveat — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/vendors/sony/SonyConnectionDelegate.kt` (SonyConnectionDelegate.kt lines 76-92 and 203-245): re-writes DD30/DD31 before every DD11 update although the document and A7C II baseline lock once then stream.
- CameraSync timezone caveat — `third_party/CameraSync/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/sebastiano/camerasync/vendors/sony/SonyProtocol.kt` (SonyProtocol.kt lines 187-199): derives packet offset fields from the host system zone rather than the supplied `ZonedDateTime` zone.
- Older A7 III protocol document — `third_party/ILCE7M3ExternalGps/PROTOCOL_EN.md` (PROTOCOL_EN.md lines 1-103): documents DD/EE UUIDs, DD21 mask, ordered DD30/DD31 setup, and a DD11 vector reproduced by the local A7C II encoder.
- Sony advertisement pairing/location status — `third_party/ILCE7M3ExternalGps/PROTOCOL_EN.md` (PROTOCOL_EN.md lines 1-27): defines known type-`0x22` support, paired, location-support, and location-enabled bits useful for sanitized live pairing diagnostics.
- ILCE7M3ExternalGps documentation error — `third_party/ILCE7M3ExternalGps/PROTOCOL_EN.md` (PROTOCOL_EN.md lines 10-18): groups raw advertisement bytes 4-5 as a two-byte protocol version even though byte 4 is version and byte 5 is reserved.
- ILCE7M3ExternalGps maintenance caveat — `third_party/ILCE7M3ExternalGps/README_EN.md` (README_EN.md lines 1-5): describes ILCE-7M3 scope and says the 2021 implementation is abandoned, reference-only, and only “seems to work.”
- ILCE7M3ExternalGps source error — `third_party/ILCE7M3ExternalGps/src/CameraBle.h` (CameraBle.h lines 51-72 and 144-170): passes payload length 93/89 as BLE write length, truncating protocol-required 95/91-byte DD11 packets by two bytes.
- ILCE7M3ExternalGps source error — `third_party/ILCE7M3ExternalGps/src/CameraBle.h` (CameraBle.h lines 51-72 and 144-170): leaves DD11 byte 5 at `0x03` when selecting the no-timezone length and never populates nonzero timezone/DST offsets.
- ILCE7M3ExternalGps source error — `third_party/ILCE7M3ExternalGps/src/CameraBle.h` (CameraBle.h lines 36-43 and 265-291): implements only DD21/DD11 and omits the documented modern DD01/DD30/DD31 flow, DD32/DD33 reads, and cleanup, while Git history shows newer endpoints were added only to documentation after source maintenance stopped.
- ILCE7M3ExternalGps source error — `third_party/ILCE7M3ExternalGps/src/ILCE7M3ExternalGps.ino` (ILCE7M3ExternalGps.ino lines 97-104): converts signed coordinates from `double` directly to `unsigned long`, so southern/western coordinates are not portably encoded as required signed 32-bit values.
- ILCE7M3ExternalGps documentation error — `third_party/ILCE7M3ExternalGps/PROTOCOL_EN.md` (PROTOCOL_EN.md line 104): calls 89 the shortened packet length even though 89 is the payload-length field and the on-wire packet is 91 bytes.
- A7C II FF00 compatibility evidence — `third_party/alpharemote/README.md` (README.md lines 18-28 and 51-53): lists A7C II among confirmed Bluetooth-remote models while explicitly stating geotagging is not implemented.
- Sony advertisement-status context — `third_party/freemote/README.md` (README.md lines 7-41) and `third_party/freemote/src/BLECamera.cpp` (BLECamera.cpp lines 225-257): provides A7 III-tested FF00 context plus manufacturer and pairing/location status-bit parsing, not DD location transfer.
- alpha-shot scope — `third_party/alpha-shot/README.md` (README.md lines 3-13) and `third_party/alpha-shot/composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/SonyCameraControl.kt` (SonyCameraControl.kt lines 201-214): implements FF00 remote triggering while geotagging remains a future goal.
- ESP32 A7 IV remote scope — `third_party/esp32-a7iv-rc/README.md` (README.md lines 1-18) and `third_party/esp32-a7iv-rc/src/main.cpp` (main.cpp lines 96-124): implements only the FF00/FF01/FF02 remote path.
- Puck.js remote scope — `third_party/puckjs-sony-remote/alpha-remote.js` (alpha-remote.js lines 35-39) and `third_party/puckjs-sony-remote/README.md` (README.md lines 91-112): implements a derivative FF00 shutter remote and provides no DD location evidence.
- nRF Connect remote scope — `third_party/sony_camera_ble_remote/README.md` (README.md lines 1-7) and `third_party/sony_camera_ble_remote/Capture.xml` (Capture.xml lines 2-16): contains FF00 shutter macros only and notes incomplete pairing/bonding work.
- Sony-PMCA-RE transport scope — `third_party/Sony-PMCA-RE/README.md` (README.md lines 1-2): uses USB for firmware/settings work and is not a BLE location reference.
- SonyAlphaUSB transport scope — `third_party/SonyAlphaUSB/README.md` (README.md lines 1-13): uses Windows USB/WIA/PTP and is not a BLE location reference.
- alphawire transport scope — `third_party/alphawire/readme.md` (readme.md lines 3-16 and 33-74): uses USB/PTP with a separate PTP/IP backend and is not a BLE location reference.
- darkgrade transport scope — `third_party/darkgrade/README.md` (README.md lines 7-23 and 147-152): implements ISO-15740/PTP over Node USB and is not a BLE location reference.
- libgphoto2 transport scope — `third_party/libgphoto2/README.md` (README.md lines 19-29): covers USB Mass Storage/PTP/MTP, so its unrelated PTP `0xDD11` occurrences are not Sony BLE location evidence.
- libptp transport scope — `third_party/libptp/README` (README lines 28-31 and 41-47): is a PTP library whose tested transport was USB, not Sony BLE location.
- remote-camera-control-rs transport scope — `third_party/remote-camera-control-rs/README.md` (README.md lines 27-45 and 57-69): validates ScalarWebAPI/PTP-IP on A7 III/A6700 and provides no Sony DD BLE location evidence.
- sony-alpha-python transport scope — `third_party/sony-alpha-python/README.md` (README.md lines 1-18): uses network PTP3 over SSH and provides no Sony DD BLE location evidence.
